declared_purpose: Manage Tencent Cloud COS objects and buckets; perform CI image, document, media, speech and content processing; manage and search MetaInsight datasets and knowledge bases; generate result previews; provide console guidance. Credential persistence is optional. Sources: SKILL.md:1–35; scripts/setup.sh:239–248.

data_operations.operation: Read credentials and configuration locally
data_operations.source: Process environment and project .env.enc or .env
data_operations.data_scope: SecretId, SecretKey, optional Token, runtime account identifiers and configuration. The loader imports all parsed assignments without an allowlist.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory and process.env
data_operations.condition: Credential resolution against process.env, in either mode. Encrypted files are tried before plaintext files, before runtime credential selection; existing nonempty environment values prevail.

data_operations.operation: Inspect local setup and return status
data_operations.source: Local executable availability, installed SDK, environment-variable presence and project files
data_operations.data_scope: Node/npm versions, dependency presence, credential-variable presence and credential-file existence; credential values are not printed by these checks.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Terminal output to the invoking caller
data_operations.condition: setup.sh --check-only; strict mode skips credential-file checks.

data_operations.operation: Install dependencies and validate COS connectivity
data_operations.source: Package manifest and configured COS bucket
data_operations.data_scope: npm dependency requests; a bucket listing requesting at most one object. Setup consumes only the success indicator from the listing output.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured npm registry, whose address is unspecified; local node_modules; COS through the SDK
data_operations.condition: Public-mode setup --from-env. This path installs dependencies and verifies connectivity even without --persist.

data_operations.operation: Persist optional plaintext credentials
data_operations.source: TENCENT_COS_* environment variables
data_operations.data_scope: SecretId, SecretKey, optional Token, bucket, region, dataset and domain configuration
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Project .env; .gitignore receives an exclusion. An existing .env.enc remains.
data_operations.condition: Public-mode setup --from-env --persist; chmod 600 is requested.

data_operations.operation: Encrypt credentials, retain a previous encrypted copy and delete plaintext
data_operations.source: Entire .env; existing .env.enc; hostname, username and package path
data_operations.data_scope: All .env contents, not only recognized COS settings; local machine/user/path attributes derive the encryption key.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: .env.enc and, when replacing an existing encrypted file, .env.enc.bak; plaintext .env is unlinked.
data_operations.condition: Public-mode encrypt-env. AES-256-GCM encryption and chmod 600 are implemented; unlinking does not establish secure erasure.

data_operations.operation: Restore plaintext credentials and provide cleanup guidance
data_operations.source: .env.enc
data_operations.data_scope: Decrypted configuration and credentials
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: .env with chmod 600; .env.enc remains. Suggested cleanup removes .env and .env.enc, but omits .env.enc.bak.
data_operations.condition: Public-mode decrypt-env; cleanup commands are instructions, not automatic deletion.

data_operations.operation: Authenticate remote requests
data_operations.source: Resolved credentials and action parameters
data_operations.data_scope: The shared client uses SecretKey locally for HMAC and transmits SecretId within Authorization, derived signatures and optional Token. The SDK receives credentials and optional Domain, ServiceDomain and Protocol settings.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Shared-client HTTPS requests initially target validated Tencent COS/CI hosts; SDK destination behavior depends on its implementation and configuration.
data_operations.condition: Authenticated business requests. SDK internals and redirect behavior are not supplied.

data_operations.operation: Upload, download and copy object content
data_operations.source: Selected local files, supplied strings or existing COS objects
data_operations.data_scope: Complete selected content, object keys, optional user metadata and copy-source addresses
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected COS bucket for uploads/copies; selected local output path for downloads. Results return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: upload, put-string, download or copy-object; bucket and region can be overridden.

data_operations.operation: Read object inventories, metadata and bucket configuration; change selected settings
data_operations.source: COS account, buckets and objects
data_operations.data_scope: Object names, sizes, times, tags, custom metadata, versions, multipart details, ACLs and bucket configuration; supplied ACL, CORS and tag settings are written.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: COS through the SDK; returned data goes to the invoking caller. These reads do not themselves enable bucket logging or inventory.
data_operations.condition: Selected list/head/configuration actions; list defaults to 100 objects and supports prefix and pagination.

data_operations.operation: Generate signed object-access links
data_operations.source: Credentials, bucket, region, object key and expiry
data_operations.data_scope: Object address and temporary signed access capability; preview signing also includes SecretId and optional Token in the URL.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller; generated previews additionally persist these URLs in HTML.
data_operations.condition: sign-url, document-preview URL generation or preview generation. Preview signing is local computation; generating a link does not itself download the object.

data_operations.operation: Process content and persist derived objects
data_operations.source: Existing COS objects and supplied watermark or speech-synthesis text
data_operations.data_scope: Transformed images, converted documents, video covers/transcodes, transcripts, synthesized/processed audio, archives and extracted files
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tencent COS/CI processing endpoints; requested output objects remain in the selected COS bucket. No automatic output cleanup is shown.
data_operations.condition: Selected processing actions; scripts explicitly specify output keys or prefixes. Some document/media jobs poll for completion.

data_operations.operation: Request recognition, moderation, hashes and image understanding
data_operations.source: COS object references, optional external image/document URLs, supplied text and image-analysis prompts
data_operations.data_scope: Content references or submitted text; returned descriptions, labels, OCR, QR contents, quality scores, moderation results and hashes
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tencent COS/CI endpoints; responses return to the caller. Submission of asynchronous jobs is observable, but service-side retention is unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Selected recognition/moderation/hash actions. image-analysis sends a Base64-encoded Custom prompt and optional detect-url in query parameters.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve EXIF and sample content for summaries
data_operations.source: Selected bucket/prefix objects
data_operations.data_scope: Sampled content, descriptions and potentially shooting time, camera model and GPS. EXIF returns both flattened and raw representations.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: COS EXIF/analysis endpoints; retrieved content and metadata remain with the caller for summarization unless separately previewed.
data_operations.condition: Explicit EXIF queries or the summary workflow. Summary guidance caps ordinary sampling at 20 files and suggests limiting large text reads.

data_operations.operation: Search datasets and retrieve inferred attributes
data_operations.source: Queries, filters, dataset names, image URIs, FaceId values and indexed media
data_operations.data_scope: Query text or image references; returned document excerpts, scores, media intervals, labels, ASR/OCR, face matches and tracks. Documented face categories include celebrity, sensitive and politician classifications.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Bucket CI dataset endpoints; compatibility actions use account CI endpoints. Results return to the caller, without a separate telemetry recipient shown.
data_operations.condition: Selected search/detail command and suitable indexed dataset. Body overrides transmit the supplied JSON instead of individually assembled fields.

data_operations.operation: Discover datasets and bindings across the account
data_operations.source: Account-level /datasets and /datasetbindings responses
data_operations.data_scope: All dataset pages and applicable binding pages, including unrelated datasets/buckets before local filtering; matching paths, states and timestamps are returned.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Account CI hosts, using each dataset's region; all fetched records temporarily accumulate in local memory.
data_operations.condition: find-datasets-by-bucket. BindCount=0 datasets are normally skipped; --scan-all overrides this. The pagination loop has no implemented page/item cap.

data_operations.operation: Create datasets, bindings, indexes and knowledge bases
data_operations.source: Supplied names, descriptions, object/bucket URIs and selected templates
data_operations.data_scope: Dataset metadata and indexable resource scope. Binding defaults to the entire configured bucket and stock indexing; knowledge-base creation also binds with Mode=1.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Account CI datasets/indexes and a COS knowledge-base bucket; documentation describes subsequent automatic document indexing.
data_operations.condition: Selected creation actions. Knowledge-base creation continues when its bucket already exists. Existing-file indexing depends on binding mode.

data_operations.operation: Probe a dataset's region
data_operations.source: Dataset name and account identifier
data_operations.data_scope: Dataset-name lookups and returned dataset metadata; a successful region is cached locally.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Account CI hosts in ap-chengdu, ap-beijing and ap-shanghai
data_operations.condition: Compatibility cos_node.mjs dataset operations when TENCENT_COS_METAINSIGHT_REGION and the in-process cache do not resolve the region. describe-dataset subsequently fetches details with statistics.

data_operations.operation: Read CI service status and change service configuration
data_operations.source: Target bucket, region and returned service status
data_operations.data_scope: CI binding and six subservice states; bucket identifiers and lifecycle configuration
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Bucket CI host for overall status and mutations; regional ci.<region>.myqcloud.com for filtered service listings; results return to caller.
data_operations.condition: Overall off/unbinding stops subqueries; noAuth skips four processing queries but still checks two asynchronous services. Service-status lists use the exact bucket and page size 1. Mutations use dedicated create/delete paths.

data_operations.operation: Request remote deletion or unbinding
data_operations.source: Selected object keys, index URIs or service configuration
data_operations.data_scope: Single/batch objects, file metadata indexes, service queues/configuration and CI bindings
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: COS/CI remote resources; responses return to caller.
data_operations.condition: Named deletion actions are available in public mode; strict mode rejects delete-named actions and DELETE requests. CI unbinding uses PUT with unbind. Physical erasure, versions and retained service records are not established.

data_operations.operation: Forward generic CI requests
data_operations.source: Supplied method, path, body and query JSON
data_operations.data_scope: Caller-selected request content; returned API data
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured bucket's CI endpoint, then the caller
data_operations.condition: ci-request; strict mode rejects DELETE, while the shown generic guards do not classify other methods by deletion semantics. Effects of unwrapped APIs remain unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Return diagnostic context
data_operations.source: Local runtime and remote responses
data_operations.data_scope: Working directory, platform, Node version, credential-presence booleans, request host/path/query, identifiers and failure-body snippets up to 4000 characters
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI stdout to the invoking caller; no independent logging/analytics destination is shown.
data_operations.condition: ci_api.mjs success, help and failure output. Request summaries retain query parameters, including encoded analysis prompts when present.

data_operations.operation: Build and persist a locally signed HTML preview
data_operations.source: Spec file, command argument or stdin; local credentials and HTML template
data_operations.data_scope: Up to 40 selected objects, signed original/thumbnail URLs, optional Token, original query wording, dataset/bucket names, first matching excerpt/face identifier, and document passwords within preview URLs
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Generated local HTML file; a recommended temporary spec file is another possible persistence boundary.
data_operations.condition: preview_gen.mjs. Generation reads inputs, signs locally and writes HTML without fetching thumbnails. HTML/spec cleanup is not implemented.

data_operations.operation: Export previews and load media in the viewer
data_operations.source: Generated HTML and its embedded URLs
data_operations.data_scope: Entire HTML, including query/excerpts and signed capabilities; displayed image content or CI-generated video/document thumbnails; original objects upon clicking links
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Host exportFile/artifact system when available; viewer browser; <bucket>.cos.<region>.myqcloud.com on media requests
data_operations.condition: Export is an explicit preview-workflow step when supported. Visible lazy images initiate requests; clicks open signed originals. Original images are used directly as image thumbnails.

data_operations.operation: Load third-party demonstration thumbnails
data_operations.source: Unchanged packaged sample result-data
data_operations.data_scope: Seven picsum.photos image requests and associated browser/network request metadata; COS signed links are separate click targets.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: picsum.photos
data_operations.condition: Opening the demonstration HTML unchanged. Normal preview generation replaces this sample result-data, so these requests are not established for generated previews.

data_operations.operation: Delegate optional dataset queries and console navigation
data_operations.source: Structured dataset scope/columns or selected console guidance
data_operations.data_scope: Dataset name/type and requested information columns; console links contain no dynamically inserted object content in the supplied guide.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Host page through invokeClient; Tencent console if explicitly opened
data_operations.condition: Host-supported dataset information queries, or user-requested console navigation. Merely returning a console link performs no migration/export/backup.

potential_excess.data_scope: Entire local credential/configuration files, including unrelated assignments
potential_excess.condition: Credential resolution reads/decrypts local files even when complete runtime credentials are already present.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Runtime authentication requires the selected credentials; fallback files support local configuration but need not supply every assignment on every path.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Use runtime credentials preferentially and retain intentional configuration defaults.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Select complete runtime credentials before reading fallback secrets; load only missing, allowlisted configuration fields when needed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve fallback behavior when runtime credentials are absent and preserve documented configuration precedence.

potential_excess.condition: Re-encryption overwrites an existing .env.enc; suggested cleanup later removes only .env and .env.enc.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Optional encrypted persistence requires a current usable credential file; an enduring previous copy is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Safely replace encrypted credentials and remove plaintext after successful encryption.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use atomic replacement without a lasting backup, or make backup retention explicit and include it in credential cleanup.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain recovery until the replacement is successfully written and validated.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Thumbnail URL embedded in local HTML and, upon export, the host artifact system and artifact readers
potential_excess.condition: A document preview item supplies password.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: CI needs the password to render an encrypted document; the preview outcome requires a thumbnail, not a retained password-bearing URL.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide the password to the authorized rendering request.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Render within a trusted execution context, embed the resulting thumbnail, and omit the password-bearing rendering URL from persisted/exported HTML.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep document rendering and original-file click access working; do not simply remove the password from the required CI request.

potential_excess.data_scope: Query wording, result URIs/excerpts, face identifiers and optional document passwords in a preview spec
potential_excess.condition: Following the recommended file-based preview invocation; no removal step is supplied.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Preview generation requires the spec input, while retaining a separate input file is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Deliver the spec reliably to the generator and produce the required HTML.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use stdin or securely remove the temporary spec immediately after generation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve correct JSON handling and any fields needed by the HTML preview.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full original image bytes rather than a bounded thumbnail
potential_excess.condition: Image-type preview items use the signed original URL as img.src; CSS only reduces displayed dimensions.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The explicit preview requirement is a thumbnail wall with click-through access to originals.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Display useful thumbnails and retain signed original links for clicks.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Locally sign a supported bounded image-thumbnail transformation for img.src while keeping the original URL as href.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve visual recognition, local signing and original access; verify transform output and metadata handling.

potential_excess.data_scope: EXIF GPS, shooting time, camera information and other metadata unrelated to semantic content
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: COS EXIF response returned to the summarizing caller
potential_excess.condition: The no-dataset summary fallback combines image-analysis with image-exif despite no relevant metadata request.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A content summary can require image understanding without requiring location or camera metadata. The same guide separately conditions EXIF on wanting objective metadata.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain sufficient descriptions of the sampled images.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Skip the EXIF action unless location, time, camera or other EXIF facts are relevant; when needed, pass onward only relevant fields.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain explicit EXIF requests, relevant metadata-based summaries and the sampling limit.

potential_excess.data_scope: All existing files in a bucket beyond the intended dataset/knowledge-base scope
potential_excess.condition: Binding omits URI/mode and inherits whole-bucket Mode=1 defaults, or knowledge-base creation reuses a nonempty existing bucket and binds it with Mode=1.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Requested retrieval requires indexing the intended resources; indexing unrelated history is not necessary for every task.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Bind the intended resources and index the history actually required.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Require explicit scope and indexing mode; validate reused buckets and use a supported prefix/filter or incremental mode when appropriate.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep stock indexing when historical retrieval is requested; a newly created empty bucket does not itself establish excess historical indexing.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated dataset lookup and metadata response
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The successful <AppId>.ci.<region>.myqcloud.com endpoint and local caller memory
potential_excess.condition: describe-dataset first discovers its region through GET /dataset and then repeats the lookup with statistics=true.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Dataset details and statistics are required; the successful preliminary lookup is a redundant action if its response can include the final requested information.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Locate the correct region and return dataset details/statistics.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Request the final required fields during discovery and reuse the successful response.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep necessary regional probes and verify that the discovery request can return equivalent statistics.

potential_excess.data_scope: Working directory, runtime details and credential-presence indicators
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CLI stdout returned to the invoking caller
potential_excess.condition: Every ci_api.mjs result, including help and failures
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Routine storage/search output does not require local filesystem context; diagnostics may require some of it.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return business results and useful errors.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Make detailed runtime diagnostics opt-in and omit or redact cwd by default.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain troubleshooting information when explicitly requested; this is caller-output minimization, not evidence of external telemetry.

potential_excess.data_scope: Browser/network request metadata for demonstration thumbnails
potential_excess.condition: The packaged demonstration HTML is opened unchanged; normal generated previews replace these sample URLs.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Demonstrating the preview layout requires example visuals, but an external image service is optional.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Show representative thumbnail cells and fallback behavior.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use embedded or local demonstration images.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the demo layout; do not attribute these third-party requests to normal generated previews.

unknowns: The supplied package was fully reviewed as source only. No execution, actual disclosures or deployed configuration were observed.
cos-nodejs-sdk-v5 and its transitive dependencies are absent. Their transport, custom-domain routing, redirects, logging, retries and credential handling cannot be fully traced.
npm registry configuration, resolved dependency versions, install hooks and installation-side retention are unspecified.
Tencent service-side retention, secondary processing, model use, indexing internals and deletion/backup semantics are undocumented here.

Host invokeClient/exportFile implementations, artifact recipients, access controls and retention are absent. Local HTML persistence and the instructed export boundary are observable; subsequent handling is unknown.
Whether credentials are temporary, least-privilege or expired cannot be established from variable names or policy instructions.
Generic non-DELETE CI requests are not checked for deletion semantics by the shown guards; actual service effects and SDK handling of such requests remain unresolved.
A narrower server-side reverse-binding lookup is not supplied. Account-wide enumeration may be necessary when no dataset is known, so its breadth alone is not classified as excess.
Supported zero-result connectivity checks, field-selective EXIF reads and equivalent statistics during region discovery require API confirmation before implementing those reductions.
Browser referrer behavior, external-image redirects and viewer caching are unspecified. No disclosure of COS result content or credentials to picsum.photos is established.
